correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northwestern opening and southeast-to-south upper descent
correspondence.finding: The original park maps show a northern headward approach to the labeled Brown River corridor. They do not establish that this is the actual selected farther-western feeder, or show how that selected opening enters the mapped trunk. This is a branch/through-link identity gap, not a demand for an exact initial vertex, every small pond or individual bank.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward upper-to-middle bend and successive joins
correspondence.finding: Below the unresolved headward approach, the park maps show the Brown River turning from its northern corridor toward the east. Map7 highlights and names the connected river course. This supports the selected upper-to-middle trunk at ordinary corridor scale; the feeder-to-trunk entry remains the separate unresolved component above.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastern middle approach to the Brown Lake setting
correspondence.finding: The selected southeastern middle approach corresponds to the mapped Brown River corridor northwest of Brown Lake. The continuous highlighted river on Map7, read with the park-setting and zoning maps, supports this connected regional reach. The source does not name every lateral tributary, and none is independently selected as an additional fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower eastward passage beside the Brown Lake basin
correspondence.finding: Maps2,3 and7 distinguish Brown Lake from Ford Lake and show the river continuing east along the northern side of the Brown Lake water complex. The selected lower eastward passage follows this same connected lake/river setting rather than detouring into the prominent southern basin. Brown Lake remains a component name, not a uniform river name. Generalized banks and subsidiary narrows do not prevent corridor-level correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Final eastward reach and western Ford Lake terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The final selected eastward reach corresponds to the mapped lower Brown River approach into western Ford Lake. Ford Lake is the supported actual receiving-water setting; the separate reversing-falls connection to Wager Bay lies farther east, beyond the selected ending. This is ordinary outlet-setting correspondence, without an exact shoreline or tidal-boundary claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Receiving water connection beyond the selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The plan’s own prose and MapA show that Ford Lake connects to Wager Bay through reversing tidal rapids. This passage is east of the selected ending and is contextual receiving-water evidence, not an added selected fragment or proof of the missing upstream links.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southwestern opening and first northeastward chain.
correspondence.finding: Graniel’s independent regional synthesis describes karst-dominated inland drainage and temporary surface water. It provides no map or locality description identifying the selected opening or connecting these first five parts as a surface river. A regional groundwater-flow direction does not establish this particular selected path.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected southern inland continuation, directional changes and intervening part joins.
correspondence.finding: No acquired source maps a named or unnamed through-channel along this inland chain. The source’s general description of a connected karst aquifer is not transferred to the rendered mainstem or its intermediate joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Central inland northward corridor and joins.
correspondence.finding: The regional hydrology chapter supplies a relevant karst setting but no corridor-scale channel, lake, cenote or managed-passage connection for these selected parts. Neither a uniform river name nor named reach identities have been established.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastward inland approach, northern turn and first northwestward approach toward the coast.
correspondence.finding: Graniel describes groundwater emerging near the north coast and supplying esteros and coastal lagoons. The two inspected coastal maps do not extend far enough inland to establish this selected approach. No particular marsh, cenote, canal or river connection is inferred from that regional process.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestward bend and northward approach to the Dzilam coastal-lagoon vicinity.
correspondence.finding: The CICY coastal-lagoon chapter establishes Dzilam as a named coastal lagoon supplied by freshwater springs and marine water. The Ahuatzin field map gives a local lagoon setting, but its limited footprint does not map the selected southern approach or establish its joins through any intervening wetlands. No managed passage is identified.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected final northward and westward bends and actual endpoint, without replacing it with a nearby mapped opening.
correspondence.finding: Figure 1 in Ahuatzin and colleagues places the selected terminal toward the lagoon’s northeastern interior and barrier margin at ordinary local-map scale. Its depicted lagoon–Gulf opening lies southwest of this terminal sector. The map therefore supports the coastal-lagoon context but does not establish the selected final chain as that opening or as a through-going Gulf outlet. Exact shoreline alignment is not asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northern opening and upper Stonecabin valley approach
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies on the upper mapped Willow Creek drainage in the northern Stonecabin valley. Plate 1 depicts the descending mountain-valley channel and tributary convergence into the southward axial trunk over these selected parts. The opening is within the same mapped drainage; a new headwater river identity is not inferred from neighboring labels.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper axial Willow Creek and shallow-groundwater valley reach
correspondence.finding: The selected continuation follows the mapped Willow Creek axial corridor past the Point Rock/Side Hill Spring surroundings and the marked evapotranspiration area toward the Stonecabin constriction. The shaded shallow-groundwater area is not treated as a lake or as proof of current surface flow.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper-to-lower Stonecabin valley bedrock passage
correspondence.finding: The selected southeastward then southward passage corresponds to the mapped Willow Creek corridor around the southern end of the internal ridge. The author describes overflow from the upper valley into the lower valley through the gaps near Stonecabin and Five-Mile Springs. This supplies a source-described surface connection in addition to the map, without requiring perennial flow or an exact bank match.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower named trunk and tributary joins
correspondence.finding: The lower selected corridor follows the mapped Willow Creek south and southwest through Stonecabin Valley, including the joins shown along that corridor. DOE explicitly identifies Willow Creek as also called Stone Cabin Creek and separately describes Stone Cabin Creek and Saulsbury Wash as converging on Mud Lake Playa. The tributary name is not imposed on the whole selected trunk.

correspondence.component_scope: Western alluvial and playa-complex approach to Mud Lake
correspondence.finding: Plate 1 depicts the lower drainage entering the westward lowland and playa complex between the Monitor Hills and Cactus Range, with Mud Lake at the western end. Eakin explicitly describes surface water moving westward through that gap toward Mud Lake, and DOE describes the corresponding named creek floodplain reaching the Mud Lake Playa system. Together the mapped corridor and authorial surface-drainage statements establish this selected connection at ordinary scale; the inference is not based on basin membership or modeled drainage alone. Individual distributary threads within the playa complex are not assigned separate names.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual Mud Lake terminal
correspondence.finding: The actual selected terminal lies within the Mud Lake playa shown on Plate 1. The terminal is part of the source-described Stonecabin-to-Mud Lake surface-drainage system. Mud Lake is retained as the terminal lake/playa name, not relabeled as a river reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southern opening and incoming passage toward Hamilton Reservoir.
correspondence.finding: The already-read partnership prose identifies a northern outlet of Mashapaug Pond as the Quinebaug headward connection. The acquired reservoir map shows southern incoming channels but does not provide enough exterior coverage to establish the actual selected initial point and its complete connection. A named regional outlet is not substituted for that missing selected link.

correspondence.component_scope: Hamilton Reservoir water-body passage within the headward selection; the listed parts are an orientation window, not exact name-boundary assignments.
correspondence.finding: The original MassWildlife map directly labels Hamilton Reservoir and its South Basin and North Basin. Both panels show the continuous water body, the open connecting passage at Causeway/Mashapaug Road, and the northern dam with an outgoing stream-flow arrow. These observations support the internal reservoir passage at ordinary map scale. They do not establish the entire exterior incoming or downstream reach covered by the orientation window.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward Holland approach, eastward Massachusetts turn and succeeding southeastward valley toward the state boundary.
correspondence.finding: The prior partnership prose places East Brimfield and Westville dams and lakes along the Quinebaug. It does not map every selected bend, the Holland approach, or the inlet-to-outlet passages of those impoundments. The unavailable guide and master plan were not inspected and supply no correspondence evidence.
bounded_component_names: East Brimfield Lake, contextual managed water body
Westville Lake, contextual managed water body

correspondence.component_scope: Northern Connecticut approach and the West Thompson/Putnam portion of the selected southward corridor.
correspondence.finding: The prior partnership prose identifies West Thompson Dam and Lake on the Quinebaug, and lists the French River at Thompson and Little River at Putnam as tributaries. This establishes named regional relationships but does not supply a readable map of the selected reservoir passage, adjacent course or actual intermediate joins.
bounded_component_names: West Thompson Lake, contextual managed water body

correspondence.component_scope: Selected middle and lower eastern Connecticut corridor toward the receiving Shetucket reach.
correspondence.finding: The prior Quinebaug page identifies tributaries at Pomfret, Canterbury, Danielson, Plainfield and Griswold, and states that the Quinebaug enters the Shetucket in Norwich. The inspected prose supports the overall river sequence. No usable corridor map was read to establish all selected intermediate segments, local impoundment passages or the selected approach to that confluence.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward lower reach and Norwich river-junction setting before the southward estuary.
correspondence.finding: The Shetucket and Thames pages expressly identify the Shetucket–Yantic junction at Norwich Harbor as the beginning of the Thames. The Shetucket page describes Greenville and Taftville among its dam sites. This is useful authorial junction and managed-setting evidence, but no inspected map establishes the selected lower-river passage through those settings or its ordinary alignment with the chosen joins.

correspondence.component_scope: Final southward estuarine portion, including the actual rendered terminal toward New London/Groton.
correspondence.finding: The Thames page describes a tidal estuary beginning at Norwich Harbor, continuing to Long Island Sound, with named tidal coves and the lower New London/Groton harbor setting. It also describes the maintained lower channel. This supports regional estuary identity, but the actual final selected segment and terminal were not compared with readable original cartography. No exact mouth position or complete terminal correspondence is claimed.
bounded_component_names: Long Island Sound, regional receiving-water context
